text:
Maria: FYI CypherBank POC — customer reporting slow first-token (their words: noticeable pause before any tokens). Started after switching to the hosted endpoint this morning. Also asking about KMS flow + an updated security questionnaire. Can SE/SRE triage?
Lee: Jumping in. Do we have a sample request + timestamps? Which model/variant are they hitting?
Maria: They sent logs, attaching snippet: `POST /v1/generate 200 OK 13:05:12 -> first_token 1.82s total 2.9s`
Devin: 1.8s FF seems high. What's their input length / sampling params? Is batching configured server-side?
Maria: Short prompts (~30 tokens). 0.9 temperature, streaming off. No custom prefill.
Sam: Could be cold KV cache or batching/queueing causing head-of-line wait. Any 429s or queueing logs?
Maria: They saw a few 429s earlier this week but not during this small run.
ops-bot: [metric alert] cypherbank-poc: prefill_cache_miss_rate=72% kv_cache_hits=28% avg_first_token=1.74s
Devin: That prefill_cache_miss_rate is the smoking gun. If prefix/KV cache misses, we pay the full decode for initial tokens. Are they pinning model versions or using an infrequent variant?
Lee: They moved from a quantized variant to a higher fidelity variant — could explain larger kernel load and slower warmup. Also check batching window: if continuous batching is on with a window we might be waiting to fill batches.
Sam: Ask them to enable `prefill:true`/`warmup:true` in the POC (we can provide a quick warmup script). Also check model variant name and sequence length — long max_seq on serving can increase kernel startup cost.
Maria: Customer asked if there's a per-request param to avoid batching wait. They want as-low-latency as possible for interactive flows.
Devin: They can set `max_batch_wait_ms=0` on dedicated, but hosted has defaults. For hosted, suggest `prefer_low_latency=true` header for the POC (we can route to low-latency tier). I'll open a routing override for their seat for the next 2 hours.
Irfan: Security Qs: CypherBank asked about KMS—does hosted ever see plaintext keys? We need a short doc snippet: key material never leaves HSM; we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private; hosted supports envelope encryption.
Maria: They also want an updated security questionnaire (SOC2 + KMS section). Can Irfan & AE own that reply?
Irfan: I'll take the KMS section. Quick note for them: hosted uses envelope encryption; customer can bring keys to Dedicated for exclusive control. I'll paste a 2‑para answer.
Sam: Back to perf — logs show frequent cache churn: their prompt prefixes vary slightly which prevents KV reuse. If their prompt template includes timestamps/session ids, that will destroy cache hits. Ask them to stable-prefix or use a placeholder token.
Lee: Good point. Recommend standardizing prompt scaffolding. I can share a small patch to their template. Also send them a warmup command:```
# warmup script (curl)
for i in {1..10}; do curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $POC_TOKEN" -d '{"model":"xlarge-v1","prompt":"<<STANDARD_PREFIX>> hello"}'; done
```
Maria: Pricing / burst question: they asked if short bursts will spike billing or if we have burst credits.
Devin: Hosted is usage-based; short bursts will bill tokens. For predictable bursts consider Dedicated reserved capacity or ask for a short-term credit. I'll loop in Sales Ops for a one-off credit.
Lee: For immediate improvement: 1) standardize prompt prefix, 2) run warmup script, 3) enable prefer_low_latency route, 4) we'll provide a short doc on KMS and send security questionnaire answers.
Maria: I'll send a consolidated note to the customer with those 4 items. Any blockers?
Sam: One more check — if they are behind a VPC with egress NAT, network jitter can add ~100-200ms. Maria, confirm their deployment topology.
Maria: They're hosted client (no VPC). Devin — can you attach the routing override ticket number once created?
Devin: Done — routing override #R-5821. Temporary low-latency routing active for their account until 2365013680.
Maria: Great, I'll reply to CypherBank with action items and ask for a short window to reproduce. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Lee: I'll DM the customer a minimal prompt template and the warmup script.
Irfan: Security questionnaire answers will be in your inbox in ~45m.
Devin: Monitoring the POC metrics, will update if we see an improvement.
Maria: Last note — customer asked about SLA for Dedicated. I'll include the Dedicated SLA doc and a rapid cost comparison (monthly reserve vs ad-hoc).
